people.name: Average adult
people.basis: About 9 years of schooling (world mean 8.8, UNDP 2025), a service-sector job, one native language plus a little of a second.

people.name: Indian engineering graduate
people.basis: Four-year B.Tech (computer science or allied branch), about five years in an IT job, typical reading and media habits.

people.name: High-IQ adult
people.basis: Master's in electrical engineering (illustrative), reads about 40 books a year across subjects. Assumed to learn roughly 1.5 to 2 times more per hour than average, but with the same hours in a day.

people.name: Elon Musk
people.basis: BA physics and BS economics, University of Pennsylvania (1997); by his account left a Stanford PhD programme within days (1995); has run SpaceX engineering as CEO and CTO since 2002; Tesla CEO since 2008; co-founded Zip2, X.com/PayPal, Neuralink, The Boring Company and xAI.

people.name: Bill Gates
people.basis: Left Harvard (1975) to co-found Microsoft, wrote much of its early software and was CEO until 2000; has led the Gates Foundation's work on global health, vaccines and development since 2000; founded TerraPower and Breakthrough Energy; books on climate (2021) and pandemic preparedness (2022).

people.name: Terence Tao
people.basis: PhD Princeton (1996); Fields Medal (2006); UCLA professor; hundreds of papers across harmonic analysis, PDEs, combinatorics, number theory, random matrices and compressed sensing; active in formal proof and AI-assisted mathematics.

people.name: Demis Hassabis
people.basis: Computer science, Cambridge (1997); game designer and programmer (Theme Park, Elixir Studios); PhD cognitive neuroscience, UCL (2009); co-founded DeepMind (2010): AlphaGo, AlphaFold; Nobel Prize in Chemistry (2024); founded Isomorphic Labs for drug discovery.

people.name: Jennifer Doudna
people.basis: PhD Harvard (1989); UC Berkeley professor; co-developed CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing (2012); Nobel Prize in Chemistry (2020); founded the Innovative Genomics Institute; co-founded several biotech companies; public work on the ethics of gene editing.

people.name: Warren Buffett
people.basis: MS economics, Columbia (1951), studying under Benjamin Graham; ran Berkshire Hathaway for about six decades (CEO until the end of 2025, chairman until September 2026); deep exposure to insurance, finance, accounting and dozens of industries; a famously heavy reader of annual reports.

people.name: Noam Chomsky
people.basis: PhD linguistics, University of Pennsylvania (1955); taught at MIT from 1955; founded generative grammar (Syntactic Structures, 1957); a central figure in cognitive science and the philosophy of language and mind; 150+ books on linguistics, politics and media.

people.name: Amartya Sen
people.basis: Schooled at Santiniketan; Presidency College, Calcutta; PhD Cambridge (1959); Nobel Prize in Economics (1998) for welfare economics and social choice; Harvard professor of economics and philosophy; books on development, justice, famine, and Indian history and culture.

people.name: Sundar Pichai
people.basis: B.Tech metallurgical engineering, IIT Kharagpur (1993); MS materials science, Stanford; MBA, Wharton (2002); worked at Applied Materials and McKinsey; led Chrome and Android at Google; CEO of Google (2015) and Alphabet (2019).

people.name: Barack Obama
people.basis: BA political science, Columbia (1983); JD Harvard (1991) and president of the Harvard Law Review; taught constitutional law at the University of Chicago Law School (1992-2004); US President (2009-2017); author of three bestselling books.

people.name: Neil deGrasse Tyson
people.basis: BA physics, Harvard (1980); PhD astrophysics, Columbia (1991); director of the Hayden Planetarium since 1996; served on US presidential commissions on the aerospace industry (2001) and space exploration (2004); hosted Cosmos (2014) and StarTalk; many popular-science books.

people.name: Ken Jennings
people.basis: BA English and computer science, BYU (2000); worked as a software engineer; 74-game Jeopardy! winning streak (2004); won the Greatest of All Time tournament (2020); Jeopardy! host since 2021; trivia and geography books. Grew up partly in South Korea and Singapore.

people.name: A. R. Rahman
people.basis: Left school to work as a musician; diploma in Western classical music on a Trinity College London scholarship; film composer across Tamil, Hindi and international cinema, working in Carnatic, Hindustani, Western classical, Sufi and electronic idioms; two Oscars and two Grammys; founded KM Music Conservatory (2008); directed Le Musk.

people.name: Yuval Noah Harari
people.basis: DPhil history, Oxford (2002), specialising in medieval and military history; professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem; Sapiens, Homo Deus, 21 Lessons and Nexus span world history, biology, economics and AI.

people.name: Devi Shetty
people.basis: MBBS, Kasturba Medical College (1979); FRCS (England) and cardiothoracic training at Guy's Hospital; 15,000+ heart operations; performed India's first neonatal heart surgery (1992); founded Narayana Hrudayalaya, now Narayana Health (2001); helped design the Yeshasvini low-cost insurance scheme.

people.name: Amitav Ghosh
people.basis: BA history and MA sociology, University of Delhi; DPhil social anthropology, Oxford (1982), with fieldwork in an Egyptian village; novels including the Ibis trilogy; nonfiction on climate change and colonial history; Jnanpith Award (2018).
